text:
Ryan Strome is in his first full season in Calgary, playing about 14 minutes a night in a middle-six role, and the assists are coming even when the goals aren't. He has 10 points in 23 games, including five assists and no goals over his last ten, and his scoring rate is right where it was last season with Anaheim.

The shooting is the soft spot: 3 goals on 46 shots, 6.5%, below the 10% to 15% range we'd expect from him. His chance quality is modest, which fits Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season: he shoots a lot, but fewer of those shots come from the slot than the volume suggests. At five on five the Flames break about even in expected goals with him on the ice and do a bit better than without him.

Evolving-Hockey had him around 0.5 wins above replacement last season, a useful depth center rather than a driver. For a fifth overall pick now past 900 games, that's the job. The thing to watch is whether he gets inside more often; that's where his goals will come from.
headline: Ryan Strome, Calgary's quiet setup man
